comparison: Both evaluations support the DUB activity findings for R438W and A451V mutations (C2, C21-C24, C26). OpenEval emphasizes the convergence of multiple complementary assays, while peer reviewers explicitly confirmed R438W is 'nearly completely DUB-dead' and A451V shows 'normal activity.' Both agree the methodology is appropriate and the evidence is strong.

Perfect agreement on STRIPAK binding deficiency of A451V (C3, C29, C30). Both evaluations support the co-immunoprecipitation findings showing selective STRIPAK-binding deficiency. Peer reviewers accepted the findings without challenge, and OpenEval noted the use of multiple STRIPAK components strengthens the conclusion.

Both support the viability and breeding data for the mouse models (C31, C33, C34). OpenEval focuses on these claims specifically, while peer review R3 also includes the cortical cell density findings (C4, C35-C42). Both evaluations acknowledge the data without concerns about the hypomorphic allele viability.

Strong agreement on cortical cell density findings (C4, C35-C42). OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative immunohistochemistry methodology with littermate controls and blinded analysis. Peer reviewers affirmed mice 'exhibit smaller neuronal and glial cell densities' and praised the validated methodology. Both acknowledge incomplete penetrance without criticism.

Perfect agreement on dopaminergic neuron deficits and motor phenotypes (C5, C43-C51). Both evaluations support the correlation between TH+ neuron loss and rotarod behavioral deficits. OpenEval notes causality is inferred rather than directly demonstrated, while peer reviewers accepted the findings as consistent with patient phenotypes.

Complete agreement on APC ubiquitylation findings (C52-C55). Both evaluations support the conclusion that both DUB and STRIPAK-binding activities are required for efficient APC deubiquitylation. OpenEval emphasizes the differential effects of the three mutants, while peer reviewers affirmed the findings without raising concerns.

Perfect agreement on APC trafficking to microtubule plus-ends (C6, C58-C67). Both evaluations support the microscopy findings including confocal and super-resolution imaging. OpenEval highlights the quantification and systematic comparison across mutants, while peer reviewers accepted the findings without challenge.

Complete agreement on axonal APC trafficking and neurite outgrowth defects (C7, C68-C72). Both evaluations support the live cell lattice lightsheet imaging findings. OpenEval emphasizes the use of endogenous APC-tdTomato and blinded analysis, while peer reviewers affirmed the findings link biochemical defects to cellular dysfunction.

Both evaluations support the mechanistic model (C8, C9, C85, C108). OpenEval notes the model is explicitly labeled as proposal/speculation but well-supported by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers accepted the model without objection, treating it as a reasonable interpretation. Both agree the model logically integrates the experimental findings.

Both evaluations rate the neural crest hypothesis as uncertain/speculative (C74-C77). OpenEval notes the hypothesis is plausible but lacks direct experimental evidence and the mouse models don't exhibit microcephaly. Peer reviewers did not comment on this speculation, neither supporting nor challenging it, consistent with its explicitly speculative nature.

Both evaluations support the background clinical information (C1, C18). OpenEval R15 covers broader background (C1, C10-C18) while peer R9 focuses on clinical associations (C1, C18, C73). Both treat these as established facts from prior literature without concerns.

OpenEval supports the integration with evolutionary conservation literature (C78-C83), including Drosophila phenotypes and independent validation of Trabid-STRIPAK interaction. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background/literature integration claims.

OpenEval supports the key integrative conclusion about parallel phenotypes (C84) from mechanistically distinct mutations providing evidence for a common pathway. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this integrative claim.
OpenEval supports the integration of prior published work (C86-C91) including unpublished data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific literature integration claims.

OpenEval rates speculative mechanistic hypotheses as uncertain (C92-C97), noting they are logical but untested, particularly regarding GSK3 inhibition rescue. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative mechanisms.
